quizzes.title: Treaty of Yandaboo and Its Legacy
quizzes.passage: Myanmar's President, Min Aung Hlaing, undertook a five-day official visit to India, his first since the 2021 political transition in Myanmar. Myanmar holds a central place in India's Neighbourhood First Policy, its Act East Policy and its wider Indo-Pacific vision. It is the only ASEAN nation that shares a land border with India, and the two countries are connected by both land and sea. The booklet describes Myanmar as a geographic bridge linking India with Southeast Asia. To understand the relationship, it helps to look at the past. For a long period, a large part of the Indian territory lying in the east was under the control of the Myanmar side. This situation changed with a treaty known as the Treaty of Yandaboo. The treaty was signed by representatives of the British and of the Myanmar side. Its signing also brought an end to a war fought between the two powers. Myanmar's position also places it close to India's island territories, which makes maritime cooperation important for regional stability. The visit's outcomes included cooperation on counter-insurgency, as Myanmar assured India that its territory would not be used by anti-India insurgent groups operating near the frontier. Both countries also discussed connectivity in the wider relationship.

questions.q: Which Indian region was under the control of the Myanmar side for a long period until the treaty?
questions.explanation: The booklet states that much of India's North-East Region was under Burmese occupation until the Treaty of Yandaboo.

questions.q: In which year was the Treaty of Yandaboo signed?
questions.explanation: The booklet dates the Treaty of Yandaboo to 1826.

questions.q: What did the Treaty of Yandaboo establish?
options: A trade agreement between ASEAN and India
questions.explanation: The booklet says the treaty established the current India-Myanmar boundary.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): The Treaty of Yandaboo established the current India-Myanmar boundary.
Reason (R): The treaty was signed on behalf of both the British and the Burmese sides.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Both statements are true, but the fact that the treaty had two signatory sides does not explain why it set the boundary.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Treaty of Yandaboo:
I. Much of India's North-East Region was under Burmese occupation until the treaty.
II. The treaty was signed in 1851.
III. The treaty established the current India-Myanmar boundary.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statement II is wrong because the treaty is dated 1826, while statements I and III match the booklet.

questions.q:
How many of the following statements about the Anglo-Burmese War are correct?
I. The Treaty of Yandaboo ended the war.
II. The war is dated 1824-1826.
III. The war was fought between the British and the Burmese side in 1851.
questions.explanation: Statements I and II are correct, while statement III gives a wrong date for the war.

questions.q: Which war did the Treaty of Yandaboo end?
questions.explanation: The booklet states that the treaty ended the Anglo-Burmese War of 1824-1826.

quizzes.title: Yandaboo Treaty Facts
quizzes.passage: Myanmar's President made a five-day official visit to India, his first since the political transition in 2021. The visit fits into India's Neighbourhood First Policy, Act East Policy and wider Indo-Pacific vision. The booklet calls Myanmar India's only ASEAN neighbour, connected to India through both land and maritime routes, and describes it as a geographic bridge to Southeast Asia. Looking back, a large part of one Indian region lay under the rule of a neighbouring kingdom for an extended period. That arrangement ended with a treaty named after a place, the Treaty of Yandaboo. Representatives of two powers signed it. The same treaty brought an end to a war fought between those powers. The visit's outcomes included security cooperation, the Kaladan Multi-Modal Transit Transport Project and the Trilateral Highway. The booklet also refers to the Rupee-Kyat settlement mechanism, which has been operational since 2024. The booklet's historical context section begins with the treaty and its effects on Indian territory, and it presents this background as the context for the present visit. Myanmar's links to India's Act East Policy are discussed in the same opening section. The booklet's account of the treaty is short, and it then moves on to the outcomes of the visit.

questions.q: In which year was the Treaty of Yandaboo signed?
questions.explanation: The booklet dates the Treaty of Yandaboo to 1826.

questions.q: In which years did the war that the treaty ended take place? (give both years)
questions.explanation: The booklet dates the Anglo-Burmese War to 1824-1826.

questions.q: Representatives of which two parties signed the treaty? (name both)
questions.explanation: The booklet says the treaty was signed on behalf of the British and of the Burmese side.

questions.q: What did the treaty establish between India and Myanmar? (one word)
questions.explanation: The booklet says the treaty established the current India-Myanmar boundary.

questions.q: Which war did the treaty bring to an end? (name)
questions.explanation: The booklet states that the treaty ended the Anglo-Burmese War of 1824-1826.

questions.q: Under whose control was a large part of an Indian region before the treaty? (one word)
questions.explanation: The booklet says much of India's North-East Region was under Burmese occupation until the treaty.

questions.q: Which Indian region was under that control before the treaty? (name)
questions.explanation: The booklet identifies India's North-East Region as the area under Burmese occupation until the treaty.

quizzes.title: Connectivity Projects and the Visit
quizzes.passage: Connectivity was one of the themes of the visit by Myanmar's President to India. The booklet lists two connectivity projects among the outcomes of the visit. The first is the Kaladan Multi-Modal Transit Transport Project, which combines different modes of transport to link India with Myanmar. The second is the India-Myanmar-Thailand Trilateral Highway, a land route that connects India with Thailand. The highway is a major road project, and it was discussed alongside the transit project during the visit. The booklet describes the transit project as a route that uses more than one mode of transport. The booklet describes Myanmar as central to India's Neighbourhood First Policy and Act East Policy. It also describes Myanmar as a link between India and Southeast Asia, and it notes that Myanmar's geographic proximity to India's island territories makes maritime cooperation important. The booklet presents both projects as part of the broader relationship between the two countries. The booklet's list of outcomes also includes educational cooperation, under which India increased the number of ICCR scholarships available to Myanmar students. The booklet also records a Rupee-Kyat settlement framework that both sides agreed to promote. The visit was the first official visit by Myanmar's President to India since the 2021 political transition.

questions.q: The Trilateral Highway passes through which country before reaching Mae Sot in Thailand?
questions.explanation: The booklet states that the highway passes through Myanmar before reaching Mae Sot in Thailand.

questions.q: What did the booklet say was announced for the Trilateral Highway during the visit?
options: Its route would be changed to avoid Myanmar
questions.explanation: The booklet states that efforts were announced to expedite the implementation of the highway project.

questions.q: What did both countries reaffirm about the Kaladan project?
options: Commitment to complete it at the earliest
questions.explanation: The booklet says both countries reaffirmed their commitment to completing the Kaladan project at the earliest.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): India and Myanmar agreed to complete the Kaladan project at the earliest.
Reason (R): Both connectivity projects were featured among the outcomes of the visit.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
questions.explanation: Both statements are true, but being featured among the outcomes does not explain the commitment to complete the project.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the connectivity projects:
I. Both countries reaffirmed commitment to complete the Kaladan project at the earliest.
II. The Trilateral Highway passes through Thailand before reaching Myanmar.
III. Efforts were announced to expedite the Trilateral Highway's implementation.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statement II reverses the route, while statements I and III match the booklet.

questions.q:
How many of the following statements about the connectivity projects are correct?
I. The Kaladan project is a multi-modal transit transport project.
II. The Trilateral Highway starts in Thailand.
III. Efforts to expedite the Trilateral Highway's implementation were announced.
questions.explanation: Statements I and III are correct, while statement II reverses the highway's route.

questions.q: The name of the India-Myanmar-Thailand Trilateral Highway refers to how many countries?
questions.explanation: The highway's name lists India, Myanmar and Thailand, which makes three countries.

quizzes.title: Connectivity Projects Recap
quizzes.passage: Connectivity was one of the subjects linked to the visit made by Myanmar's President to India. The visit's outcomes included two connectivity projects. The first is a multi-modal transit transport project, which combines different modes of transport to link India with Myanmar. The second is a trilateral highway that connects India, Myanmar and Thailand by road. The highway begins on the Indian side, runs into Myanmar and continues on to Thailand. The booklet describes Myanmar as central to India's Neighbourhood First Policy and Act East Policy, and it describes the country as a link between India and Southeast Asia. Both countries discussed the transit project during the visit, and the highway was also part of those discussions. Myanmar's regional importance, as the booklet explains, rests on its land and maritime links with India. The booklet also mentions an assurance from Myanmar that its territory would not be used by anti-India insurgent groups. The booklet lists both projects among the outcomes, and it presents them as part of the broader relationship between the two countries, which also covers security cooperation and the Indo-Pacific vision. The visit was the first official visit by Myanmar's President to India since the 2021 political transition, a point the booklet states at the start of its coverage.

questions.q: Which Thai town does the Trilateral Highway reach? (name of town)
questions.explanation: The booklet says the highway passes through Myanmar before reaching Mae Sot in Thailand.

questions.q: What did the visit's outcomes announce for the Trilateral Highway? (two words)
questions.explanation: The booklet states that efforts were announced to expedite the implementation of the highway.

questions.q: The booklet describes Myanmar as a geographic ___ linking India with Southeast Asia. (one word)
questions.explanation: The booklet describes Myanmar as a geographic bridge linking India with Southeast Asia.

questions.q: The Trilateral Highway runs from the border at Tamu to which two Myanmar towns? (name both)
questions.explanation: The booklet says the highway runs from the Tamu-Moreh border to Kalemyo and Kalewa.

questions.q: What did both countries reaffirm about the multi-modal transit project? (phrase)
questions.explanation: The booklet says both countries reaffirmed their commitment to completing the project at the earliest.

questions.q: What is the name of the multi-modal transit transport project? (one word)
questions.explanation: The booklet names the multi-modal transit transport project as the Kaladan Multi-Modal Transit Transport Project.

questions.q: Myanmar is India's only neighbour in which regional grouping? (acronym)
questions.explanation: The booklet calls Myanmar India's only ASEAN neighbour.

quizzes.title: Myanmar's Takeover and Its Aftermath
quizzes.passage: Myanmar has experienced a sharp change of control in recent years. The army took over the government after alleging huge irregularities in a parliamentary election held in November. Troops seized a city hall just ahead of the announcement, and the army then declared a state of emergency. Elected civilian leaders were taken into custody before the new parliament could convene. Communication services were restricted, and banks were closed across the country. A former general who was serving as vice president was set to become the acting head of state. The party that had secured two landslide victories in democratic elections was among those affected by these events. The booklet presents these events as what we know so far, and it lists them in a short timeline that starts with the allegations about the polls. The army's announcement was followed by a period of restricted communications and closed banks, as the timeline records. Several civilian politicians were held in the days that followed, according to the same account. Myanmar's current President has since made his first official visit to India after this change. The booklet describes that visit as a five-day official trip, and it notes that it was his first visit to India since the transition.

questions.q: Who was to become acting president after the takeover?
questions.explanation: The booklet names Myint Swe, a former general and the vice president, as the person to become acting president.

questions.q: On which date did the military seize power in Myanmar?
questions.explanation: The booklet dates the military's seizure of power to February 1, 2021.

questions.q: For how long did the army declare the state of emergency?
questions.explanation: The booklet states that the army declared a one-year state of emergency.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): The military took power in Myanmar in 2015.
Reason (R): The NLD won landslide victories in 2015 and 2020.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Assertion A is false because the takeover was in 2021, while the NLD landslide victories in 2015 and 2020 are correct.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. Myint Swe   ->   A. Declared a state of emergency after the takeover
II. Aung San Suu Kyi   ->   B. Won landslide victories in 2015 and 2020
III. National League for Democracy   ->   C. Former general and vice president
IV. The army   ->   D. Taken into custody hours before parliament convened
questions.explanation: Myint Swe was the former general and vice president, Aung San Suu Kyi was taken into custody, the NLD won the landslide victories, and the army declared the emergency.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the takeover:
I. The army declared a state of emergency after the takeover.
II. Banks were kept open nationwide during the takeover.
III. Myint Swe was a former general and the vice president.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statement II is wrong because banks were closed nationwide, while statements I and III match the booklet.

questions.q:
How many of the following statements about the takeover are correct?
I. Communication services were restricted across the country.
II. Win Myint was the President who was detained.
III. Myint Swe was the sitting President before the takeover.
questions.explanation: Statements I and II are correct, while Myint Swe was the vice president, not the sitting President.

quizzes.title: Takeover Timeline Quiz
quizzes.passage: Myanmar's recent political history has been marked by a sudden change of control. The army moved against the elected government after alleging serious irregularities in a parliamentary election that had been held in November. Troops took over a key government building just ahead of the announcement, and the army then declared a state of emergency across the country. Elected civilian leaders were taken into custody hours before the new parliament was due to convene. The sitting President was among those detained. Communication services were restricted across the country, and all banks were closed nationwide. A former general who had served as vice president was positioned to take over as acting head of state. The booklet presents these events under the heading What we know so far, and the timeline it gives begins with the army's allegations and continues with the custody of leaders and the restrictions that followed. Myanmar's current President has since undertaken his first official visit to India since this transition, a five-day official trip. The booklet also notes the army's own account of why it acted, namely the alleged irregularities in the polls. Earlier elections had been won by the National League for Democracy, which secured landslide victories. The booklet's timeline therefore links the earlier electoral period with the takeover that followed.

questions.q: Who was to become acting president? (name)
questions.explanation: The booklet names Myint Swe, a former general and the vice president, as the person to become acting president.

questions.q: On which date did the military seize power? (give the full date)
questions.explanation: The booklet dates the military's seizure of power to February 1, 2021.

questions.q: How long did the army's state of emergency last? (in years)
questions.explanation: The booklet states that the army declared a one-year state of emergency.

questions.q: Which civilian leader was taken into custody hours before parliament was due to convene? (name)
questions.explanation: The booklet says Aung San Suu Kyi and other civilian leaders were taken into custody hours before parliament was due to reconvene.

questions.q: Which President was detained along with the civilian leaders? (name)
questions.explanation: The booklet names President Win Myint as one of those detained with the civilian leaders.

questions.q: Which key building did troops seize just ahead of the announcement? (two words)
questions.explanation: The booklet says troops seized the city hall just ahead of the announcement.

questions.q: Which kind of services were restricted across the country? (one word)
questions.explanation: The booklet states that Internet and mobile phone communications were severely restricted across the country.
